authority.abi: C ABI unchanged; no export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, method-table slot or CRYPTO_* seam coordinate changed
external_contracts: A BIO callback (including the connect BIO's info callback and a free callback installed on an inner datagram BIO) must not free or otherwise invalidate the BIO or its method data while a dispatch operation is in progress. Reused from boundary sweep B1.

A BIO_MSG array passed to BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg contains num_msg records spaced stride bytes apart; each data pointer is readable/writable for data_len bytes and each non-NULL peer/local pointer is a live BIO_ADDR. The methods do not validate this layout.
Caller-supplied out-parameters (msgs_processed, int*, BIO**, BIO_ADDR*, timeval*, BIO_POLL_DESCRIPTOR*) are writable and non-NULL wherever the authority writes them unconditionally.
BIO_CTRL_DGRAM_SET0_LOCAL_ADDR transfers ownership of the BIO_ADDR exactly once; the caller must not pass the incumbent pointer, and must not free the transferred value.
BIO_C_GET_CONNECT returns pointers borrowed from the connect context; they remain valid only until the next SET_CONNECT, RESET or BIO_free.

A datagram BIO is not internally synchronised and must not be freed, reset or re-controlled concurrently with an in-flight read/write. A datagram pair synchronises only its ring buffers; ctrl mutations (mtu, caps, local_addr, buffer size) are not serialised against data operations (authority parity).

boundaries.mechanism: context lifecycle: dgram_pair_init, dgram_mem_init, dgram_pair_free, CtxDestroy for BioDgramPairSt through OwnedCtx
residuals: dgram_pair_free leaves bio.ptr dangling after dropping the context (authority parity); a second destroy is therefore caller UB, and the core's single-destroy reference gate is the enforcing contract.
The context is zalloc'd and only published to bio.ptr after the lock allocation succeeds; the zero-state sweep executes destroy_body on an all-zero block.

boundaries.mechanism: RingBuf allocation/resize/release over CRYPTO_malloc/realloc/free
residuals: head_tail/push_pop rely on the internal invariant idx[i] <= len and count <= len; the authority's ossl_assert checks are not reproduced.
ring resize trusts the preconditions checked by its callers (growth only, or empty for shrink); the moved tail offset is nbytes - len, valid only on growth.

boundaries.mechanism: pairing/unpairing: BIO_C_MAKE_BIO_PAIR, BIO_C_DESTROY_BIO_PAIR, peer pointers and local_addr ownership
residuals: Pairing does not reject bio1 == bio2 (authority parity). Reads on such a self-pair fail because the two-lock helper's second write_lock reports the same-thread re-acquisition as 0; they do not deadlock.
Only the half being freed releases its own local_addr; the peer's address is released by the peer's own free, so freeing one half also unpairs the other.
The port nulls local_addr after BIO_ADDR_free (the authority does not), which removes the authority's destroy-pair-then-free double-release; this is a deliberate safety improvement.

boundaries.mechanism: shared read/write locks, role-ordered two-lock acquisition, pending and write-guarantee locking
residuals: The authority's role-distinctness asserts are omitted; the port's CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock returns 0 for a same-thread write re-acquisition, so the reachable self-pair case fails cleanly instead of deadlocking.
mtu, cap, local_addr and req_buf_len are mutated by ctrl without taking the ring lock (authority parity); concurrent ctrl with data operations is an external precondition.

boundaries.mechanism: datagram framing read/write, truncation and rollback, ring-growth arithmetic

defects.severity: low (panic/lock-leak via caller-supplied size; contract-violating length)
defects.class: unchecked length sum used as the ring-growth allocation target
defects.detail: dgram_pair_write_inner computed req_buf_len + sz unchecked. This crate builds with overflow-checks = true, so a hostile BIO_MSG.data_len that overflows panics while the caller holds the pair write lock; guard_ffi converts the panic to an error but leaves the lock held. Without overflow checks the target wraps and can leave the growth loop spinning.
defects.repair: checked_add; an unrepresentable target is treated as 'no space', so the existing rollback path runs and the lock is released.
defects.control: authority differential (the C authority has the same unchecked addition) plus source review; no runtime pre-fix canary was executed.

residuals: sz/data_len remains a caller-trusted length; the valid-buffer precondition is not validated (authority parity).
dgram_pair_ctrl_pending omits the authority's l == sizeof(hdr) assertion; on an impossible partial-header state it returns a header-derived length instead of 0 (no out-of-bounds access).
A failed header or body write restores idx[0]/count but not a grown req_buf_len; capacity changes are not part of the observable datagram state.

boundaries.mechanism: strided BIO_MSG batches, address slots and message-result publication
residuals: msg_at forms i * stride unchecked; the caller's array contract (num_msg records stride bytes apart) is the precondition, and num_msg is clamped to 64 before use.

boundaries.mechanism: BIO_s_dgram_pair, BIO_s_dgram_mem, BIO_new_bio_dgram_pair exports and method tables
residuals: BIO_new_bio_dgram_pair tolerates a NULL pbio1/pbio2 by leaking that half (the authority writes unconditionally); output slots are caller-writable.

boundaries.mechanism: BioConnect lifecycle, owned hostname/service strings, owned address chain, inner datagram BIO
residuals: conn_free releases the context only when a.shutdown != 0 (authority parity); a caller that clears shutdown leaks the context and leaves ptr live.
The inner datagram BIO is released before the context, so a free callback installed on it runs while the connect context is still valid; re-entry into BIO_free is absorbed by the core reference gate.

boundaries.mechanism: socket descriptor ownership and the connect state machine (CREATE_SOCKET, CONNECT, BLOCKED_CONNECT, close)
residuals: Descriptor close/shutdown follows b.shutdown and the OK state; concurrent use of the BIO while freeing is an external precondition (authority parity).

boundaries.mechanism: inner BIO delegation (read/write/ctrl/mmsg), create_dgram_bio, BIO_CTRL_DUP
residuals: BIO_CTRL_RESET does not clear dgram_bio (authority parity); a datagram connect BIO reset and reconnected may replace the inner BIO and leak the old one.
BIO_C_GET_DGRAM_BIO returns the inner BIO borrowed; the application must not free it while the connect BIO owns it.

boundaries.mechanism: info-callback reentrancy edge in conn_state
residuals: The callback is invoked with raw b/c pointers and no Rust reference or lock is held across it; the B1 BIO-callback non-invalidation contract is the external precondition. A callback that frees the BIO makes the subsequent context use a use-after-free (authority parity).

boundaries.mechanism: ctrl ownership and out-parameters: SET_CONNECT, GET_CONNECT, GET_PEER/DETECT_PEER_ADDR, GET_DGRAM_BIO, GET/SET_CALLBACK, DUP
residuals: GET_CONNECT/GET_CALLBACK return borrowed internal pointers; callers must not use them after the next mutation or free.

GET_PEER/DETECT_PEER_ADDR pass num to memcpy as a size; a negative num becomes a huge size_t (authority parity, upstream FIXME). Output pointers are dereferenced where the authority requires non-NULL.

boundaries.mechanism: conn_sendmmsg/conn_recvmmsg delegation to the inner datagram BIO
residuals: msgs_processed is dereferenced unconditionally by the method; the public BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg wrapper guarantees non-NULL, and the array contract is delegated unchanged.

boundaries.mechanism: BIO_s_connect and BIO_new_connect exports
residuals: BIO_new_connect(NULL) succeeds with no name, because SET_CONNECT leaves ret = 1 for a NULL pointer (authority parity).

boundaries.mechanism: BioDgramData lifecycle: dgram_new, dgram_free, dgram_clear, empty CtxDestroy
residuals: dgram_free leaves bio.ptr dangling after OwnedCtx releases the block (authority parity).
dgram_clear closes the descriptor only when both shutdown and init are set, and resets init/flags without touching connected/peer (authority parity).

boundaries.mechanism: descriptor ownership: BIO_new_dgram, BIO_C_SET_FD/GET_FD, reset
residuals: BIO_new_dgram ignores the BIO_int_ctrl(SET_FD) result, so an invalid descriptor still yields an initialised BIO (authority parity).
BIO_C_SET_FD dereferences ptr as int* unconditionally; the control's pointer contract is the external precondition.

boundaries.mechanism: embedded peer/local BIO_ADDR storage and address ctrl copies
residuals: BIO_CTRL_DGRAM_CONNECT/SET_PEER/SET_CONNECTED/GET_PEER/DETECT_PEER_ADDR read or write caller-owned BIO_ADDR/sockaddr memory; the pointer and length are caller obligations.
GET_PEER/DETECT_PEER_ADDR pass a negative num to memcpy as a huge size_t (authority parity, upstream FIXME).

boundaries.mechanism: receive-timeout bracket and setsockopt/getsockopt controls
residuals: SET_NEXT_TIMEOUT and SET/GET_RECV/SEND_TIMEOUT dereference caller timeval pointers unconditionally; timer arithmetic intentionally wraps/saturates as the authority does.

boundaries.mechanism: read/write/puts, retry flags, unconnected-peer capture
residuals: outl/inl are c_int lengths passed to libc; the public BIO_read/BIO_write wrappers reject non-positive values, while the raw method contract trusts its caller.
A successful unconnected read records the sender through the SET_PEER ctrl; the BIO has no internal lock (authority parity).

boundaries.mechanism: message translation and ancillary data: translate_msg, extract_local, pack_local, Batch, msg_at
residuals: BIO_MSG data/peer/local pointers and lengths are caller-owned; the kernel-written cmsg length is trusted when reading ancillary payloads.
msg_at forms i * stride unchecked under the caller's array contract; num_msg is clamped to 64.
num_processed is dereferenced unconditionally by the method; the public mmsg wrapper guarantees non-NULL. BIO_CMSG_ALLOC_LEN is pinned by unit tests against cmsg_space.

boundaries.mechanism: BIO_s_datagram and BIO_new_dgram exports
residuals: The descriptor is caller-owned unless close_flag is non-zero; the close ownership transfers to the BIO exactly once.
